findings.title: Sensitive card data (PAN, CVV/CVC/CAV2/CID, track/magstripe) appears to be passed to a logger. PCI DSS 3.2 prohibits storing CVV at all, and PAN must be masked (display first-6 + last-4 only). Mask or drop the value before logging.
findings.description: Sensitive card data (PAN, CVV/CVC/CAV2/CID, track/magstripe) appears to be passed to a logger. PCI DSS 3.2 prohibits storing CVV at all, and PAN must be masked (display first-6 + last-4 only). Mask or drop the value before logging.

exploit.payload: Login as alice, POST /api/payments/charge with marker PAN=4111111111111111 CVV=123, then GET /api/payments/logs and search for the PAN/CVV markers
exploit.expected_signal: The /api/payments/logs response contains the unmasked PAN '4111111111111111' and CVV '123' that we submitted
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: Unmasked PAN/CVV in logs: charge user=alice pan=4111111111111111 cvv=123 amount=1.23
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: Unmasked PAN/CVV in logs: charge user=alice pan=4111111111111111 cvv=123 amount=1.23

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Removes CVV from the log entirely (PCI DSS 3.2 forbids storing CVV/CVC/CAV2/CID in any form, including logs) and masks the PAN to first-6 + last-4 before logging, satisfying PCI DSS PAN display requirements. The masking helper is inlined as a local function so no new external symbols are introduced and the change is self-contained.
references: OWASP A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

findings.title: Payment-gateway callback handler trusts amount from the request without re-fetching the authoritative amount from your DB. Webhook callers can be spoofed (or replayed with altered values) -- always reconcile against your own order record before marking the order settled.
findings.description: Payment-gateway callback handler trusts amount from the request without re-fetching the authoritative amount from your DB. Webhook callers can be spoofed (or replayed with altered values) -- always reconcile against your own order record before marking the order settled.

exploit.payload: POST /api/webhook/gateway with orderId=order-1001 and amount=0.01 to spoof the gateway callback and settle a $75.00 order for $0.01 without any server-side reconciliation
exploit.expected_signal: GET /api/payments/order/order-1001 returns amount=0.01 and status=settled after the webhook call
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: order order-1001 settled at tampered amount=0.01 (original=75.0); server accepted spoofed webhook without reconciliation
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: order order-1001 settled at tampered amount=0.01 (original=75.0); server accepted spoofed webhook without reconciliation

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Instead of trusting the webhook's amount field and overwriting the authoritative order amount, the patch reconciles the incoming amount against the order record already in the database. If the values disagree, the request is rejected with a 400 and the order is not settled; only when the amounts match is the order marked settled. This prevents spoofed/replayed webhooks from tampering with the settlement amount.
references: OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures

findings.title: Account/order/payment record is fetched by a caller-supplied id with no ownership check. Classic IDOR -- User A can read User B's account by changing the URL parameter. Verify the authenticated user owns the resource before returning it (e.g. UserId == User.GetUserId()).
findings.description: Account/order/payment record is fetched by a caller-supplied id with no ownership check. Classic IDOR -- User A can read User B's account by changing the URL parameter. Verify the authenticated user owns the resource before returning it (e.g. UserId == User.GetUserId()).

exploit.payload: Login as alice, then GET /api/account/bob using alice's Bearer token to read bob's balance (IDOR — no ownership check)
exploit.expected_signal: HTTP 200 with JSON body containing id=bob and bob's balance returned to alice
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: alice's token read bob's account — id=bob balance=500
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: alice's token read bob's account — id=bob balance=500

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Resolves the token to the authenticated username and enforces an ownership check: the account id requested in the URL must match the user bound to the bearer token. Any mismatch returns 403 Forbidden, preventing IDOR where Alice's token reads Bob's account.

findings.title: Payment-mutating endpoint persists a transaction/charge without checking for an Idempotency-Key header against a dedup store. Network retries and double-clicks will create duplicate charges. Require Idempotency-Key, persist (key -> response) with a TTL, and return the cached response on replay.
findings.description: Payment-mutating endpoint persists a transaction/charge without checking for an Idempotency-Key header against a dedup store. Network retries and double-clicks will create duplicate charges. Require Idempotency-Key, persist (key -> response) with a TTL, and return the cached response on replay.

exploit.payload: Authenticate as seeded user alice then POST /api/payments/transfer twice with identical body and no Idempotency-Key header
exploit.expected_signal: Two successful responses return different transaction_ids for the same request body, proving replay/duplicate charge is accepted
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: duplicate transfers created without Idempotency-Key tx1=c9f6a7d333814d4a tx2=7f922db91b364480
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: duplicate transfers created without Idempotency-Key tx1=c9f6a7d333814d4a tx2=7f922db91b364480

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: The transfer endpoint now requires an Idempotency-Key header and consults a per-user dedup store (ConcurrentDictionary on PaymentsStore) with a 24h TTL. On replay within the TTL window we short-circuit and return the originally cached transaction_id/amount instead of persisting a new TxRecord, preventing duplicate charges from network retries or double-clicks. Missing keys are rejected with 400 so callers cannot bypass the guard. Uses only existing in-scope symbols (ctx, auth, db, req) plus a new IdempotencyRecord type and IdempotencyKeys field added to PaymentsStore via extra_edits; System.Collections.Concurrent is already imported.
